data.one_liner: Restrict a Windows app to a single instance and bring existing windows to the front.
data.what_it_does: Forces a single instance of your Windows app, bringing the existing window to the front when a new instance is opened. It allows passing startup arguments and an optional callback when a second instance tries to launch.
use_when: You want to prevent users from opening multiple instances of your Windows desktop app
You need to bring the existing application window to the foreground when a secondary launch is attempted
avoid_when: Your application targets mobile, web, or non-Windows desktop platforms exclusively
You want to allow multiple independent instances of your app to run simultaneously
strengths: Brings the correct window to the front even if it is minimized
Supports passing custom arguments and exit functions to secondary instances
Simple and straightforward setup in the main function
weaknesses: Functionality is not supported on web even though it builds
data.setup_notes: Add WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized() and make main async, then call WindowsSingleInstance.ensureSingleInstance() with arguments and a unique custom app string.
